question: Should OpenClaw install a fail-closed pre-push guard for all contributor checkouts, or keep this as an advisory command outside the default Git lifecycle?
rationale: The implementation can be wired mechanically, but deciding whether a repository-wide local hook may block established contributor push workflows is a compatibility and contributor-policy choice.

options.title: Adopt a lifecycle guard
options.body: Wire the checker into the existing hook installation path with a documented, tested remote-selection contract and redacted real-push evidence.

options.title: Keep an advisory tool
options.body: Retain a manually run diagnostic command, but remove claims that it automatically prevents unsafe publication.

options.title: Pause core integration
options.body: Decline the repository-wide hook and route any local publishing safety workflow to contributor tooling outside the default checkout.

recommendation.title: Adopt a lifecycle guard
recommendation.body: Wire the checker into the existing hook installation path with a documented, tested remote-selection contract and redacted real-push evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns repository-wide contributor and package-hook behavior; no more specific current-main owner was established from the available history.
